chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Hisham ibn Salim said:

Khattab al-A'war asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) while I was sitting, saying: 'There was a hired worker at my father's place who worked for wages, and we lost him, and some of his wages remained for him, and we do not know his heir.' He said, 'Seek him.' He said, 'We have sought him but did not find him.' He said, 'Poor men,' and moved his hands. He repeated to him, saying, 'Seek and strive. If you can find him, [pay him]; and if you cannot find him, it is like your own property until a claimant comes to him. And if an incident befalls you, bequeath it; if a claimant comes to him, let it be paid to him.'

key_terms.سَبِيلُ مَالِكَ: Like your own property (treated as owned but conditional)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for the wages of a missing hired worker?
ai.summary: This narration from the chapter on the inheritance of the missing person (al-Mafqud) establishes the principle of conditional ownership, where the employer holds the wages as a trust pending the worker's reappearance or the emergence of an heir. The Imam’s instruction to 'seek and strive' emphasizes the diligence required in verifying the status of the missing individual before finalizing the transfer of assets, reflecting the Shia juristic approach to balancing certainty with precaution in financial trusts.
